output.brief:
Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump came from the storage compaction tuning change pushed on the evening of 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. In every cell that got the config push, p99 rose within minutes of it, whatever its gateway rollout time. In aps-3, the one cell that skipped the push, 5.8 is running and p99 stayed at about 94 ms. A test rollback to 5.7 in euw-1 changed nothing (291 to 297 to 293 ms). On the storage nodes, compaction threads went from 2 to 6, disk use from 41% to 97%, and node-side read time from 61 to 262 ms. The network and traffic growth don't explain it. A rollback would also reopen the security hole and wouldn't fix latency.

Next step: revert the tuning in one cell and watch p99 and compaction backlog. If that works, extend the revert to the other cells. Don't pause compaction fleet-wide, because backlog would grow and disks could fill. Pacing Orrin's ingest is premature: backlog is 4% and wasn't traced to Orrin alone, since a lifecycle sweep also contributed. Attribution is due 10 Nov. I'm fairly confident (about 90%).
